q: Under the BP 220 IRR, what is the minimum frontage of a single-detached corner lot?
n: The BP 220 IRR sets a lower minimum frontage of 8 m for single-detached corner lots in economic and socialized housing. Source: BP 220 IRR (Revised), minimum lot frontage table.

q: How much allocation, in percent of gross area, is required for parks and playgrounds at a density of 21–25 DU/ha?
n: At 21–25 dwelling units per hectare, the PD 957 IRR requires 4.0% of gross area for parks and playgrounds. Source: PD 957 IRR (Revised 2008), parks and playgrounds allocation table.

q: How much allocation, in percent of gross area, is required for parks and playgrounds at a density of 36–50 DU/ha?
n: At 36–50 dwelling units per hectare, the PD 957 IRR requires 6.0% of gross area for parks and playgrounds. Source: PD 957 IRR (Revised 2008), parks and playgrounds allocation table.

q: How much allocation, in percent of gross area, is required for parks and playgrounds at a density of 51–65 DU/ha?
n: At 51–65 dwelling units per hectare, the PD 957 IRR requires 7.0% of gross area for parks and playgrounds. Source: PD 957 IRR (Revised 2008), parks and playgrounds allocation table.

q: What is the minimum percentage of gross area for parks, playgrounds and recreation in an open market subdivision?
n: In an open-market subdivision the minimum allocation for parks, playgrounds and recreation is 3.5% of gross area, at 20 DU/ha and below, rising with density. Source: PD 957 IRR (Revised 2008).

q: Under PD 957, what is the minimum lot area for a single detached unit in an open-market subdivision?
n: Under the PD 957 IRR, the minimum open-market lot area for a single-detached unit is 120 m². Duplexes need 96 m² and row houses 60 m². Source: PD 957 IRR (Revised 2008), minimum lot area table.

q: Under PD 957, what is the minimum lot area for a duplex in an open-market subdivision?
n: Under the PD 957 IRR, the minimum open-market lot area for a duplex (single-attached) unit is 96 m². Source: PD 957 IRR (Revised 2008).

q: Under PD 957, what is the minimum lot area for a row house in an open-market subdivision?
n: Under the PD 957 IRR, the minimum open-market lot area for a row house is 60 m², the smallest open-market lot type. Source: PD 957 IRR (Revised 2008).

q: Under the BP 220 IRR, what is the minimum lot frontage of a regular lot for single-detached housing?
n: The BP 220 IRR requires a minimum frontage of 8 m for a regular single-detached lot in economic and socialized housing. Source: BP 220 IRR (Revised), minimum lot frontage table.

q: Under PD 957, what is the minimum open market frontage for a regular lot?
n: Under the PD 957 IRR, a regular single-detached lot in an open-market or medium-cost subdivision needs at least 10 m frontage. Corner lots need 12 m. Source: PD 957 IRR (Revised 2008).

q: For projects of what size or more must area be set aside for parks and playgrounds, treated as non-buildable?
n: Subdivision projects of 1 ha or more must set aside area for parks and playgrounds, treated as non-buildable and non-saleable. Source: PD 957 IRR (Revised 2008); PD 1216.

q: Percentage of saleable area in a subdivision.
n: Because at least 30% of the gross area must stay as open space (roads, parks, facilities), saleable lots may take at most 70% of a subdivision. Source: PD 1216 (amending PD 957, Sec. 31); PD 957 IRR.

q: Under PD 957, at least what share of a subdivision of one hectare or more must be open space?
n: PD 1216 requires subdivisions of 1 ha or more to reserve at least 30% of gross area as open space, including roads, parks, playgrounds and community facilities. Source: PD 1216 (amending PD 957, Sec. 31).

q: Which law governs economic and socialized housing design?
n: BP 220 governs the design of economic and socialized housing, with lower minimum standards than PD 957 to make housing affordable. Source: BP 220 and its Revised IRR.

q: Which housing is built and financed by private developers as a business and sold at market prices and interest?
n: Open-market housing is built and financed by private developers as a business and sold at market prices and interest rates. Source: PD 957 IRR (definitions).

q: Which housing serves lower-income families with lower interest and longer amortization?
n: Economic and socialized housing serves lower-income families on affordable terms, with lower interest and longer amortization. Source: BP 220 IRR; RA 7279 (UDHA), Sec. 3.

q: What is a wall shared by two dwelling units, also called a party wall?
n: A common (party) wall stands on the shared lot line and is shared by two adjoining dwelling units. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, definitions; BP 220 IRR.

q: What is a unit for one family with space for living, sleeping, cooking and eating?
n: A dwelling unit is a unit for one family, with space for living, sleeping, cooking and eating. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, definitions; PD 957 IRR.

q: Basic subdivision design.
n: The gridiron, a rectangular grid of streets and blocks, is the basic subdivision layout because it is simple and efficient to survey and sell. Source: Lynch & Hack, Site Planning; De Chiara & Koppelman, Site Planning Standards.

q: Which feature makes a subdivision lot most saleable?
n: A lot with a lake view commands the highest price. Views and amenities add value, while steep slopes and narrow frontage reduce it. Source: Appraisal Institute, The Appraisal of Real Estate.

q: The process in which a piece of land, referred to as the parent tract, is subdivided into two or more parcels.
n: Subdivision divides a parent tract of land into two or more parcels or lots. Source: PD 957, Sec. 2; De Chiara & Koppelman, Site Planning Standards.

q: Usually, the last stage of the final site development process prior to the issuance of a building permit.
n: The final plat, the approved subdivision map with lots, blocks and roads, is usually the last stage of site development before building permits are issued. Source: De Chiara & Koppelman, Site Planning Standards.

q: A tract registered under Act 496, divided mainly into residential lots and offered to the public for cash or installment sale, is a:
n: PD 957 defines a subdivision project as a tract registered under Act 496, divided mainly into residential lots and offered to the public for sale in cash or by installment. Source: PD 957, Sec. 2(d).

q: An entire property divided mainly into residential condominium units, with its structures, is a:
n: PD 957 defines a condominium project as an entire property divided mainly into residential condominium units, with its structures. Source: PD 957, Sec. 2(g); RA 4726 (Condominium Act).

q: Which written agreement gives a buyer a set period to investigate a property before deciding?
n: An option to buy is a written agreement that gives a buyer a set period to investigate a property before deciding, usually for an option fee. Source: Civil Code of the Philippines, Art. 1324 and 1479.

q: If you are going to build a structure near a body of water in Manila, where would you ask permission?
n: Building near rivers, lakes or the sea involves foreshore areas and Water Code easements, which fall under the DENR (foreshore lease and permits). Source: PD 1067 (Water Code), Art. 51; DENR DAO on foreshore areas.

q: Who approves CLUP?
n: Under EO 72 (1993) and RA 11201, the DHSUD (formerly HLURB) reviews and ratifies the CLUPs of provinces, HUCs and independent component cities. Component city and municipal CLUPs are approved by the provincial board. Source: RA 11201 (DHSUD Act) & IRR; EO 72 s.1993.

q: Which government agency handles land registration?
n: The Land Registration Authority (LRA) handles land registration and the issuance of titles, through the Registries of Deeds. Source: PD 1529 (Property Registration Decree); EO 292.

q: Which agency regulates noise pollution from industrial facilities?
n: The DENR, through its Environmental Management Bureau, regulates noise from industrial facilities under PD 984 and the NPCC noise standards. Source: PD 984 (Pollution Control Law); DENR-EMB.
